Correcting the factorization:
\[
3906=2\cdot 3^2\cdot 7\cdot 31,
\]
so \(N(5)\) has only \(4\) distinct prime factors, not \(5\). Thus \(b=5\) fails.

For \(b\ge 6\), if \(N(b)\) had \(b\) distinct prime factors, then \(N(b)\ge P_b\), the product of the first \(b\) primes. But
\[
N(6)=9331<30030=P_6,
\]
and for \(b\ge 7\), \(P_b>b^6>N(b)\) (base \(P_7=510510>7^6\), then inductively \(P_{b+1}\ge 19P_b>19b^6>(b+1)^6\)). So no \(b\ge 6\) works.

Therefore the only valid values are \(b=2,3,4\), and their product is
\[
2\cdot 3\cdot 4=24.
\]

\[
\boxed{24}
\]
